tickets.title: Feed: Inline poll voting directly on news cards
tickets.description:
Users currently have to navigate away from the Feed to vote on polls — they either swipe through to the poll in the feed (if the INSIGHT_INTERVAL triggers) or go to the Markets > Polls tab. This friction kills engagement. The poll question and YES/NO buttons should live inline on the NewsFeedCard for stories that have a linked poll, so users can vote without leaving the feed.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. In `apps/mobile/src/components/news-feed-card.tsx` (or wherever NewsFeedCard is defined), check if `item.poll` is non-null and `item.poll.status === 'OPEN'`.
2. If yes and the user has NOT yet voted (`item.poll.userVote` is null), render a compact inline poll panel at the bottom of the card: the poll question (`item.poll.title`), a YES/NO vote bar (reuse the existing bar component from PollCard), and YES/NO tap targets.
3. Tapping YES or NO calls `mobileApi.castVote(item.poll.id, { side })`. Apply optimistic update immediately: show the updated vote distribution and the 'You voted YES/NO' chip inline.
4. If the user has already voted, show the result bar + 'You voted X' chip without the vote buttons.
5. On vote success call `onVoted?.()` to trigger a feed refresh so the insight card data also updates.
6. If `item.poll.marketType === 'NUMERIC'`, show a compact number input + Submit button instead of YES/NO buttons.
7. Ensure the poll panel does not overflow the card viewport (use `maxHeight` or a collapsed/expanded toggle if needed).
8. Handle error state: if the vote API call fails, revert the optimistic update and show a brief error message.

tickets.title: Market detail: sticky betting panel (bottom sheet or fixed footer)
tickets.description:
The market detail screen (`apps/mobile/src/app/market/[id].tsx`) requires the user to scroll all the way past market info, existing positions, resolution rules, and comments to reach the betting panel. This is backwards — the primary CTA (Place Bet) should be immediately reachable. Move it to a persistent bottom-of-screen position.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Extract the betting panel (side selection, amount presets, place bet button) into a fixed-position footer or a bottom sheet (modal overlay) in `market/[id].tsx`.
2. For OPEN non-poll markets: show a persistent bottom bar with the current YES probability, a 'Predict' button, and the user's current position summary if they have one. Tapping 'Predict' opens the full betting sheet (bottom sheet or modal).
3. For OPEN poll markets: show a compact bottom bar with the poll question abbreviated and YES/NO tap targets. Voting inline collapses the bar to show the result.
4. For CLOSED/RESOLVED markets: the bottom bar shows the outcome (e.g. 'Resolved YES') and a Share Result button if the user had a position.
5. The ScrollView main content should NOT be padded with the betting panel content anymore — the information (description, stats, resolution rules, comments) fills the scroll area naturally.
6. The sticky panel must clear the tab bar and iPhone home indicator (use `SafeAreaView` insets).
7. When the bet is successfully placed: the bottom bar updates to show 'Position: YES — 100 pts' without requiring a full scroll.

tickets.title: Onboarding: first-run tooltip walkthrough for new users
tickets.description:
New users land on the Feed with no understanding of what polls vs. markets are, how points work, or what the streak means. There is no onboarding. This is the single biggest activation blocker — users who don't understand the product in the first 60 seconds do not return. Build a lightweight tooltip-based first-run walkthrough that fires exactly once for new users.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Use `AsyncStorage` to persist a `onboarding_complete` boolean. Check on app launch.
2. For users where `onboarding_complete` is not set (first run), show a 4-step tooltip overlay sequence:
   - Step 1 (Feed tab): 'Swipe up through today's news. Every story has a prediction attached.' with a pulsing arrow pointing at the first card.
   - Step 2 (first poll card): 'Tap YES or NO to vote. Your accuracy score improves with each correct prediction.'
   - Step 3 (Markets tab): 'Stake virtual points on outcomes you believe in. Top predictors earn reputation and badges.'
   - Step 4 (Profile tab): 'Track your points, accuracy, and streak here.'
3. Each step has a 'Next' button and a 'Skip' link.
4. After step 4 (or on Skip), set `onboarding_complete = true` in AsyncStorage.
5. Tooltips use a semi-transparent backdrop with a highlight cutout on the relevant UI element (use a simple modal overlay approach — no need for a native spotlight library).
6. The walkthrough can be re-triggered from Profile settings for users who want to replay it (add a 'Replay tutorial' option in the profile actions card).
7. Do not block the UI after the walkthrough completes — the app should be fully interactive immediately.

tickets.title: Streak and daily engagement mechanic
tickets.description:
The user object already has a `streak` field but it is only displayed passively on the Profile screen. It has no behavioral effect in the product — there is no reward for maintaining a streak, no warning when a streak is about to break, and no daily prompt to engage. Streaks are one of the most effective daily retention mechanics in habit-forming apps (Duolingo, Wordle). We need to make the streak mean something.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. On app launch (in `apps/mobile/src/providers/session-provider.tsx` or the root layout), fetch the user's profile and check `user.streak` and `user.lastPredictionAt` (or equivalent field).
2. If the user has a streak >= 3 AND they have NOT yet made a prediction today: show a full-screen streak reminder modal on launch. Content: 'Your X-day streak is at risk! Make a prediction today to keep it alive.' with a 'Go Predict' CTA that navigates to the Feed tab and a 'Later' dismiss option.
3. If the user's streak just broke (previous streak > 0, current streak is 0 or reset): show a single-time 'Streak reset' notification inside the app (a banner or modal, not a push notification). 'Your streak reset. Start a new one today!'
4. Add a streak indicator to the Feed tab header — a small fire emoji + streak count badge next to the category filter bar (visible only if streak >= 2). Tapping it navigates to the Profile screen.
5. If the user's streak is >= 7: add a special 'Weekly streak' visual treatment — gold border on the streak badge, different color.
6. The streak reminder modal should only fire ONCE per day even if the app is opened multiple times. Use AsyncStorage to track the last time it was shown.
7. Backend: verify that the `streak` field on the user profile updates correctly when a vote or position is placed. If the API does not return `lastPredictionAt`, add it to the `GET /api/profile/me` response so the client can compute 'has predicted today'.

tickets.title: Sports tab: tap a match to see linked markets and create a prediction
tickets.description:
The Sports tab shows live scores for cricket and football. This is valuable context — but it's a dead end. Users look at a match, get excited about the outcome, and have no path to stake a prediction. The tab should be the entry point to sports prediction markets, not just a scoreboard widget.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. In `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/sports.tsx`, make each match card tappable.
2. When a match is tapped, open a bottom sheet or navigate to a new screen that shows:
   a. The match summary (teams, current score, status)
   b. Any existing open prediction markets linked to this match. Query `GET /api/markets/public?q=<team names>&category=SPORTS` — use both team names as the search terms.
   c. A 'Create Prediction' button that pre-fills the Create tab wizard: visibility=PUBLIC, category=SPORTS, and seeds the title with e.g. 'Will [Team A] beat [Team B]?'
3. If no markets are found for the match: show an empty state with the 'Create Prediction' CTA prominently.
4. The linked markets list should show standard MarketSummaryCard items, tappable to go to market detail.
5. The 'Create Prediction' button should use the existing router navigation to `/(tabs)/create` with prefill params. If the Create screen does not support URL params for prefill, add support for reading `initialTitle` and `initialCategory` from `useLocalSearchParams`.
6. Ensure the bottom sheet or nested screen works correctly with the tab bar layout (use a modal stack if needed).

tickets.title: Profile: P&L summary card — net points won/lost across resolved markets
tickets.description:
The profile screen shows wallet balance, reputation score, accuracy %, and streak. But it does not show the one number every prediction market user cares most about: am I up or down overall? Without a P&L view, users cannot evaluate their own skill, which removes a critical engagement driver (wanting to 'get back to even' or 'protect the gain'). This is the financial feedback loop that makes prediction markets addictive.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. In `apps/api/app/api/profile/me/route.ts` (or the profile API), add a computed `pnl` field to the response:
   - `totalStaked`: sum of all `amount` across all resolved positions the user has taken.
   - `totalReturned`: sum of all `payout` values from resolved positions (if payout is stored) OR compute as: for winning positions, payout = amount * (total pool / winning pool); for losing positions, payout = 0.
   - `netPnl`: totalReturned - totalStaked (can be negative).
   - `resolvedMarketCount`: count of resolved markets the user participated in.
2. In `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx`, add a 'P&L Summary' card below the header card:
   - Show: Net P&L (large number, green if positive, red if negative), Total Staked, Total Returned, Markets Played.
   - If `resolvedMarketCount === 0`: show 'No resolved predictions yet. Start predicting to see your P&L.'
3. The card should be visually prominent — this is the first thing a returning user wants to see after their wallet balance.
4. Display amounts with the `formatPoints()` utility already in `@predict-future/utils`.
5. Add a `lastUpdatedAt` timestamp to the card so users know the data is fresh.

tickets.title: Share a market: native share sheet with deep link URL
tickets.description:
The market detail screen has a 'Share this market' link and a 'Share Result' button that both call `Share.share()` with plain text messages. These work, but do not include a deep link URL, which means recipients land on the web with no path to the specific market. Deep links are the viral loop of a prediction market — every share should bring one new user into the product with context already provided.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Update `shareOpenMarket()` in `market/[id].tsx` to include a deep link: `https://predictfuture.app/markets/${marketId}`. The share message should be: `'"${title}" — what do you think? Predict on Predict Future: https://predictfuture.app/markets/${marketId}'`
2. Update `shareMarketResult()` to also include the deep link: after the result line, append `\n\nhttps://predictfuture.app/markets/${marketId}`
3. Add a share button to the MarketSummaryCard component (small share icon, top-right corner). Tapping it triggers `shareOpenMarket`. This makes markets shareable from the Markets tab list view too.
4. Add share capability to poll cards: after voting, show 'Share your vote' — a share action that says 'I voted [YES/NO] on "[poll title]" — what do you think? https://predictfuture.app/polls/${pollId}'
5. Ensure the shared URL is valid even if the web page is not yet fully built (a basic 404 is acceptable — the URL itself is what matters for virality tracking).
6. Add `Share` import from `react-native` in any file that needs it.

tickets.title: Markets tab: sort controls and trending markets surface
tickets.description:
The Markets tab currently shows all public markets sorted by `new`. There is no way to sort by activity, volume, or closing soon. Users who want to find the most interesting open market have to scroll a chronological list. This is a discovery failure that increases time-to-first-bet for new users. The API already supports multiple sort modes — the UI just needs to expose them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. In `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/markets.tsx`, add a sort control row below the search bar (only visible in public/Explore mode, hide in search mode).
2. Sort options: 'New' (default, sort=new), 'Trending' (sort=rank), 'Closing Soon' (sort=close_at), 'Most Active' (sort=volume).
3. The active sort is highlighted. Switching sort options triggers a refetch of `mobileApi.getPublicMarkets({ sort: selectedSort })`.
4. Add a 'Trending' shelf at the top of the markets list (before the category pills) in the default/New view only: a horizontal scroll row showing the top 3 markets by `marketRankScore`. Each card in the shelf is compact (title + probability or avg prediction + participant count + category badge). Tapping navigates to market detail.
5. The trending shelf uses `mobileApi.getPublicMarkets({ sort: 'rank', limit: 3 })` — a separate fetch that can be done in parallel with the main list.
6. The sort control row should be styled consistently with the existing status tab row (same pill/chip style).
7. The category filter pills should remain below the sort row — the hierarchy is: mode toggle > search bar > sort row > status tabs > category pills > list.

tickets.title: Groups tab: replace placeholder with functional group browse and join flow
tickets.description:
The Groups tab in `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/groups.tsx` currently renders a placeholder screen with scaffolding notes. This is a nav tab that does nothing — users who tap it get a text description of what it 'will' do. This destroys trust. The full Groups API is built (GET /api/groups, POST /api/groups/join, GET /api/groups/[id]). The tab needs to be functional.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Replace the placeholder body in `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/groups.tsx` with a real screen.
2. Show two sections when authenticated:
   a. 'My Groups': a list of groups the user belongs to, fetched via `mobileApi.getMyGroups()`. Each row shows group name, member count, market count, and a right-arrow to navigate to `/group/[id]`.
   b. 'Discover Groups': a list of public groups fetched via `GET /api/groups?public=true` (add this query param support to the API if not already there, returning groups with visibility=PUBLIC or equivalent, limited to 20). Each row shows group name, description, member count, and a 'Join' button.
3. 'Join' button calls `POST /api/groups/join` with `{ inviteCode }`. Since public groups may not require an invite code, also support joining by group ID directly — add `POST /api/groups/join` to accept either `{ inviteCode }` or `{ groupId }` (whichever the API already supports; check the route handler).
4. There is also a 'Join by code' input at the top of the screen — a text field + 'Join' button. The user pastes an invite code, taps Join, and is taken to the group detail page if successful.
5. The group detail page `apps/mobile/src/app/group/[id].tsx` should already exist; verify it renders correctly (shows group name, markets list, members count). If it is a placeholder, implement the basic view using `mobileApi.getGroupById(id)`.
6. Show an unauthenticated state ('Sign in to join groups') for logged-out users.
7. Add a 'Create Group' button that navigates to `/(tabs)/create` — the Create tab already has group creation in its wizard.

tickets.title: Resolution payoff: win/loss modal with points delta when a market resolves
tickets.description:
When a user returns to a market that has resolved in their favour, the current experience is: a grey status chip says 'Resolved YES', and a Share Result button appears. That's it. There is no celebration for winning, no consolation for losing, and no clear communication of how many points were earned or lost. The resolution payoff is the emotional peak of a prediction market — it should feel like a slot machine payout, not a status update.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. In `apps/mobile/src/app/market/[id].tsx`, after fetching market data, detect when the market has just transitioned to RESOLVED status for a user who held a position:
   - Compute `wonOrLost`: check `market.winningSide` vs `userPositions[0].side`.
   - Compute the payout: for a win, estimate payout from the pool math already in `calcEstimatedReturn`. For a loss, payout = 0.
2. Show a `Modal` overlay when the above condition is first detected (use a `useRef` to track whether the modal has been shown this session, so it only fires once per app session per market).
3. Win modal content:
   - Large green checkmark icon.
   - 'You won!' headline.
   - '+[payout] pts' in large green text.
   - Subtext: 'Predicted [YES/NO] correctly on: [market title]'
   - Two buttons: 'Share Result' (triggers `shareMarketResult`) and 'Close'.
4. Loss modal content:
   - Red X icon.
   - 'Market resolved [YES/NO]' headline.
   - 'You predicted [the other side]' subtext.
   - One button: 'Close'. No points delta shown (losing 0 is implicit).
5. Do NOT show the modal if the user arrives at an already-resolved market fresh from a deep link or cold navigation (only show it if the market was OPEN when the screen loaded and then resolved, OR if there is a `justResolved=true` flag in navigation params).
6. After closing the modal, update the sticky bar to show the resolution outcome chip as it does today.

tickets.title: Notifications: make each notification tappable and route to the relevant screen
tickets.description:
The notifications screen (`apps/mobile/src/app/notifications.tsx`) renders a FlatList of notification cards. Each card shows title, body, and timestamp. Tapping does nothing. The `ApiNotification` type already includes an `href` field (e.g. `/markets/[id]`). The product needs notifications to be deep-link aware: tapping a 'Your market resolved' notification should open that market.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. In `apps/mobile/src/app/notifications.tsx`, wrap each notification card in a `Pressable`.
2. On press, parse the `notification.href` field:
   - If `href` matches `/markets/[id]`, navigate to `router.push('/market/[id]')`.
   - If `href` matches `/groups/[id]`, navigate to `router.push('/group/[id]')`.
   - If `href` is null or unrecognised, do nothing (card is still pressable but navigation is a no-op).
3. Add a visual affordance for tappable notifications: a right-facing chevron icon on the right side of each card that has a non-null href.
4. Mark a notification as read (call `PATCH /api/notifications/read` with the individual notification ID, or at minimum optimistically mark it visually) when tapped. Currently the API only supports mark-all-read; if a per-notification read endpoint doesn't exist, add `PATCH /api/notifications/[id]/read` to `apps/api/app/api/notifications/` that marks a single notification read.
5. Distinguish read vs unread notifications visually: unread cards get the left blue border (already done), read cards are fully neutral. After tapping, the left border should disappear immediately (optimistic).
6. Add a notification count badge on the Profile tab icon. This is already done in `_layout.tsx` (the `useNotificationBadge` hook is live). Verify it correctly fetches `unreadCount` from the API and displays the badge. If any bug exists, fix it here.

tickets.title: Leaderboard tab: restore as a full-screen dedicated tab visible in the nav
tickets.description:
The leaderboard screen (`apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/leaderboard.tsx`) is fully built — it has category filters, medal rankings, and per-entry accuracy stats. But the tab is hidden via `href: null` in `_layout.tsx` and buried as a collapsed accordion inside the Profile screen. This makes it invisible to the vast majority of users. The leaderboard is a critical social proof and competition driver — it should be a first-class tab.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. In `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx`, change the leaderboard tab from `href: null` to a visible tab entry with icon `trophy-outline` from Ionicons and label 'Ranks'.
2. Position the Leaderboard tab between 'Markets' and 'Profile' in the tab order: Feed | Sports | Create | Markets | Ranks | Profile.
3. In `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/leaderboard.tsx`, ensure the screen renders the full leaderboard with:
   a. A header: 'Leaderboard' title + 'Top predictors by reputation' subtitle.
   b. Category filter chips (All, Sports, Business, Tech, General) — already implemented, verify they work.
   c. The current user's own rank highlighted if they are in the top 50 (already partially implemented — verify the `isCurrentUser` detection works against the session username).
   d. If the current user is NOT in the top list, show a 'Your rank: #X' banner at the bottom — add a `userRank` field to `GET /api/leaderboard` response: query the user's rank position from the `UserStat` table and return it alongside the `entries` array.
4. Remove the embedded leaderboard accordion from the Profile screen (`apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx`) — the `LeaderboardSection` component is no longer needed there. Replace it with a simple 'See Leaderboard' link that navigates to the new tab.
5. The leaderboard should auto-refresh when the tab is focused (use `useFocusEffect`).

tickets.title: Public user profiles: tap a username anywhere to view their stats
tickets.description:
The app has no way to view another user's public profile. You can see usernames in comments on market detail pages, and in the leaderboard, but tapping them does nothing. There is already a `GET /api/profile/[username]` endpoint and an `ApiUserProfile` type. This is the social layer of a prediction market — seeing that a top predictor has 94% accuracy on tech markets should inspire competition and drive engagement.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Create a new screen at `apps/mobile/src/app/user/[username].tsx`.
2. On mount, call `GET /api/profile/[username]` (use `mobileApi.getUserProfile(username)` — add this method to the API client in `packages/api-client/src/index.ts` if it doesn't exist: `getUserProfile(username: string) { return request<ApiUserProfile>('/api/profile/' + username); }`).
3. Render the public profile:
   a. Header card: username, level tag, streak badge (if streak > 0), reputation score bar.
   b. Stats row: Accuracy %, Total Predictions, Reputation Score.
   c. Badges section: same badge pill shelf used in the own-profile view.
   d. Category breakdown bars (accuracy by category) — if `categoryStats` is returned by the API.
   e. Recent public markets created by this user (from `user.createdMarkets`, tappable to market detail).
4. Make usernames tappable in the CommentsSection of `apps/mobile/src/app/market/[id].tsx`: tapping `@username` navigates to `/user/[username]`.
5. Make leaderboard entries tappable in `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/leaderboard.tsx`: tapping a row navigates to `/user/[username]`.
6. The screen must handle the case where the username does not exist (404 from API) — show an error state.
7. Show a back button (Expo Router Stack header) — do NOT add this to the tab bar.

tickets.title: Create market: post-submission success screen and draft recovery UX
tickets.description:
The Create tab wizard (`apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/create.tsx`) submits a market and then does nothing visible to confirm success. The user doesn't know if their market was created, is pending review, or failed silently. Additionally, the AsyncStorage draft saving exists in code but users have no indication a draft was saved or how to recover it. Both of these gaps create anxiety and drop-off in the creation funnel.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. After a successful `POST /api/markets/create` call in the Create wizard, instead of silently resetting the form, navigate to a success state within the same screen (or a brief modal):
   - Success state content: a checkmark icon, 'Market Created!' headline, the market title, and the market status (e.g. 'Pending review — we'll notify you when it's approved').
   - Two CTAs: 'View Market' (navigates to `/market/[id]` using the returned market ID) and 'Create Another' (resets the form).
2. If the market is PUBLIC and status is OPEN (auto-approved), show: 'Your market is live!' with a 'Share it' button that triggers `shareOpenMarket(title, id)`.
3. Draft recovery: on mount of the Create screen, if AsyncStorage key `draft_market_form` is non-empty, show a banner at the top of Step 1 ('You have a saved draft') with a 'Restore Draft' button and a 'Dismiss' link. Tapping 'Restore Draft' loads the saved form state into the wizard. Tapping 'Dismiss' clears the draft key.
4. The draft save should happen automatically after each step (currently implemented — verify it actually writes to AsyncStorage correctly and that the restore reads back all the required fields: title, description, category, visibility, marketType, closeAt preset, resolveAt preset).
5. Show a 'Saved' indicator (small grey text 'Draft saved') that appears briefly (2s) after auto-save on each step transition.

tickets.title: Feed: skeleton loading cards on initial load instead of a blank spinner
tickets.description:
The Feed screen shows a centered ActivityIndicator while the initial page loads. On a slow connection or cold API start, this can take 1-3 seconds — users see a blank screen with a spinner, which feels broken. Skeleton cards (grey shimmer placeholders that match the shape of a NewsFeedCard) dramatically improve perceived performance and establish spatial context before content arrives.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Create a `SkeletonFeedCard` component in `apps/mobile/src/components/` that renders a static card-shaped placeholder matching the approximate layout of a `NewsFeedCard`: a tall card with a grey rectangle for the image area, two shorter grey bars for the headline and kicker, and a grey bar for the poll panel at the bottom. Use the existing `colors.border` and `colors.surface` tokens for the placeholder colors.
2. Add a shimmer animation using React Native's `Animated` API: a translucent white bar that sweeps left-to-right across the card on a 1.2s loop using `Animated.loop` + `Animated.timing`.
3. In `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/feed.tsx`, when `loading === true` AND `items.length === 0`, render a FlatList of 3 SkeletonFeedCard items instead of the `centerState` ActivityIndicator. Each skeleton card should have the same `cardHeight` as real cards.
4. Do NOT show the skeleton on subsequent loads (pull-to-refresh or pagination) — only on the first load when the list is empty. The existing RefreshControl spinner is fine for pull-to-refresh.
5. The skeleton must not flash if the API responds in under 150ms — add a 150ms delay before showing the skeleton (use a `useEffect` with a timeout that sets a `showSkeleton` boolean, cleared if data arrives first).

tickets.title: Market detail: resolution rationale and resolver identity in the resolved view
tickets.description:
When a market is RESOLVED, users see the outcome chip and can share the result. But they have no idea why the market resolved that way — who resolved it, what evidence they cited, or whether there was a challenge. This matters for host trust: a market that resolves with no explanation erodes confidence in the platform. The resolution data exists in the API response (`marketResolution` relation on the Market model).

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Ensure `GET /api/markets/[marketId]` returns the resolution details when the market is RESOLVED. Specifically, include in the response:
   - `resolution.rationale` (the text explanation the host provided)
   - `resolution.resolvedBy.username` (who resolved it)
   - `resolution.createdAt` (when it was resolved)
   - `resolution.wasOverturned` (boolean, if an admin overturned the original resolution)
   If these fields are not currently returned, add them to the market detail API handler in `apps/api/app/api/markets/[marketId]/route.ts`.
2. In `apps/mobile/src/app/market/[id].tsx`, in the `MarketBody` component, add a 'Resolution' section below the market stats for RESOLVED markets:
   - Show: 'Resolved [YES/NO]' outcome badge, resolution date, and resolver username ('Resolved by @username on [date]').
   - If `resolution.rationale` is non-empty: show the full rationale text in a card below. Label it 'Resolution Rationale'.
   - If `resolution.wasOverturned`: show an 'Overturned by admin' badge.
3. Do NOT show this section for non-resolved markets.
4. Style the rationale card consistently with the existing description/rules cards in the MarketBody.

tickets.title: Fix feed userVote persistence: add auth:true to getNews API client call
tickets.description:
**Bug:** Every feed refresh wipes vote indicators for authenticated users. `getNews()` in `packages/api-client/src/index.ts` calls the `/api/news` route without passing `{ auth: true }`, so the Bearer token is never sent. The server route at `apps/api/app/api/news/route.ts` calls `getUserIdFromRequest()` to personalize results (added in S8-T2) — but only receives the token if the client sends it. Without the token, `userId` is null and every item returns `userVote: null`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. In `packages/api-client/src/index.ts`, find the `getNews` method (or equivalent function that calls `/api/news`). Add `{ auth: true }` (or the equivalent options object field your `request()` helper uses to attach the Authorization header) to that call.
2. Verify in `apps/api/app/api/news/route.ts` that `getUserIdFromRequest(request)` is called and its result is passed into the query that populates `userVote` on each news item. If the personalization block is missing or gated behind a condition that skips it for GET requests, fix it so the userId is used whenever the token is present.
3. After the fix: when a logged-in user casts a YES vote on a poll in the feed, then pulls to refresh, the vote indicator (result bar + 'You voted YES' chip) must persist. It must NOT revert to the unvoted state.
4. For unauthenticated users (no token): behavior is unchanged — `userVote` remains null and the YES/NO vote buttons are shown.
5. No regression: the feed must still load correctly for logged-out users (no 401 errors, graceful null handling).

tickets.title: Fix Profile Bets tab: wire real positions or remove the dead tab
tickets.description:
**Bug:** `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx` renders `<PredictionsSection positions={[]} />` — a hardcoded empty array literal. The Bets tab inside PredictionsSection will always show an empty state regardless of what positions the user holds. Meanwhile, `RecentPositions` (also on the Profile screen) already displays real bet history from the API. The two components are duplicates in purpose and one is broken.

**Decision: pick ONE of the following two options and implement it fully. Do not do a partial fix.**

**Option A — Wire real data:**
1. Fetch the user's positions from the API on profile screen mount (e.g. `GET /api/positions` or whatever endpoint `RecentPositions` already uses).
2. Pass the real positions array into `<PredictionsSection positions={realPositions} />`.
3. Ensure `PredictionsSection` renders the positions correctly in its Bets tab (it likely already has the UI; it just needs real data).
4. Remove the `RecentPositions` component from the profile screen if it now duplicates PredictionsSection's Bets tab.

**Option B — Remove the Bets tab from PredictionsSection:**
1. Remove the Bets tab (and any tab switcher) from `PredictionsSection` entirely, leaving PredictionsSection to show only the Predictions tab (or whatever non-positions content it has).
2. `RecentPositions` remains as the canonical bet history display on the Profile screen.
3. Remove the `positions` prop from `PredictionsSection`'s interface since it is no longer needed.

**Acceptance criteria (both options):**
- The Profile screen must not contain any component that receives a hardcoded empty array as its primary data prop.
- A user who has placed bets must see those bets somewhere on their Profile screen.
- No duplicate display of the same data.

tickets.title: Deep-link group join: /join/[inviteCode] mobile route + web stub + app config
tickets.description:
**Goal:** A share link like `https://predictfuture.app/join/[inviteCode]` lands a recipient on a single confirmation screen showing the group name and a 'Join' button. One link, one tap, in the group.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**Mobile route:**
1. Create `apps/mobile/src/app/join/[inviteCode].tsx`.
2. On mount, call `GET /api/groups/preview?inviteCode=[inviteCode]` to fetch the group name, member count, and description without requiring auth. If this endpoint does not exist, add it to `apps/api/app/api/groups/` — it should return `{ name, description, memberCount }` for a valid invite code, and 404 for an invalid one.
3. Show a confirmation screen: group name (large), description, member count, and a single prominent 'Join Group' button.
4. Tapping 'Join Group':
   - If the user is authenticated: call `POST /api/groups/join` with `{ inviteCode }`, then navigate to `/group/[id]` on success.
   - If the user is unauthenticated: navigate to the sign-in screen with a `returnTo=/join/[inviteCode]` param so after login they are redirected back to complete the join.
5. Show a loading state while the preview fetch is in-flight and an error state if the invite code is invalid (expired or not found).

**App config (deep link):**
6. In `apps/mobile/app.config.js` (or `app.json`), ensure the scheme `predictfuture` is registered and that the path `/join/*` is included in the intentFilters (Android) and associatedDomains (iOS) config.
7. Verify the Expo Router file-system route `apps/mobile/src/app/join/[inviteCode].tsx` is picked up automatically — no manual linking config needed beyond the scheme.

**Web stub:**
8. Create `apps/web/app/join/[inviteCode]/page.tsx` (or equivalent in the web app's router). This page shows a minimal 'Open in the Predict Future app' banner with a deep link button (`predictfuture://join/[inviteCode]`) and, for users without the app, a link to the App Store. This page does NOT need full functionality — it is a redirect stub for web recipients of the share link.

tickets.title: Profile screen: surface Leaderboard and Groups links above the empty-state walls
tickets.description:
**Problem:** The Profile screen currently buries the Leaderboard and Groups navigation links below large empty-state walls (badges, predictions, positions sections that show zero data for new users). A new user sees empty sections before they ever find out there is a leaderboard or community groups. This is a discovery failure for the product's two strongest social hooks.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. In `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx`, move the Leaderboard link and Groups entry point to appear immediately after the stats/header card — above any badges, predictions, or positions sections.
2. Implement a compact inline Groups preview at the top of the profile body (before any accordion sections): show a horizontal scroll row of the user's group memberships (group name + member count chips). If the user is in 0 groups, show a single 'Find Groups' CTA chip that navigates to the Groups tab. This replaces or supplements the buried `GroupsAccordion`.
3. The Leaderboard link should be a visually prominent row (icon + 'See Leaderboard' text + chevron + optionally the user's current rank) — not a collapsed accordion. Tapping it navigates to the Leaderboard tab (`/(tabs)/leaderboard`).
4. The existing `GroupsAccordion` and `LeaderboardSection` (if still present after S8-T4) should be removed from the lower sections of the profile screen to avoid duplication.
5. The reordering must not break the existing header card, P&L card, or stats row — those stay at the very top in their current position.

tickets.title: Create wizard: Simple vs Advanced split to collapse power-user steps
tickets.description:
**Problem:** The Create tab wizard at `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/create.tsx` is currently 6 steps deep and exposes host-settings concepts (commission rate, grace period, challenge window, bond cap) to every user including first-timers. These are power-user levers that overwhelm the median user and increase wizard abandonment. The median user wants: pick a topic, write a question, set a close date, done.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**Simple path (default):**
1. Collapse the wizard to 4 steps in Simple mode:
   - Step 1: Audience (PUBLIC / PRIVATE / GROUP) — unchanged.
   - Step 2: Question type (Binary YES/NO or Numeric) — unchanged.
   - Step 3: Question text + description — unchanged.
   - Step 4: Close date (preset options: 1 day / 1 week / 1 month / custom) — unchanged.
   - After Step 4: submit directly with sensible defaults for all host-settings fields (commission=0, grace period=24h, challenge window=48h, bond cap=default).
2. The step indicator at the top of the wizard must reflect 4 steps, not 6.

**Advanced toggle:**
3. On Step 4 (or a dedicated transition screen after Step 4), show an 'Advanced settings' disclosure row (chevron, grey text: 'Set commission, challenge window, and bond cap'). Tapping it expands Step 5 (host settings) inline OR navigates to an additional step — your choice, but it must not appear by default.
4. If the user taps 'Advanced settings', show the current Step 5 host-settings fields (commission slider, grace period input, challenge window input, bond cap input) before the final submit.
5. The Advanced toggle state should persist within the session (if the user goes back and forward, the toggle stays open if they opened it).

**Validation:**
6. Simple mode submit must pass the same validation as the current wizard — title required, close date required, etc.
7. The existing draft save/restore (implemented in S8-T6) must continue to work for both Simple and Advanced modes — the saved draft must restore to the correct step and mode.

tickets.title: QA process: add mandatory smoke-test checklist to every QA report
tickets.description:
**Problem:** QA reports across Sprints 7 and 8 performed only static code checks (file existence, type correctness, import presence). No report included a manual walkthrough of the core user flow, which means bugs like the userVote persistence failure (S9-T1) and the hardcoded empty positions array (S9-T2) shipped undetected through 'passing' QA. The QA agent cannot run the app, but it can produce a deterministic checklist the human must walk through before a sprint is marked complete.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Open `.claude/agents/qa-engineer.md` and add a new mandatory section titled '## Smoke-Test Checklist Requirement'.
2. The section must state: 'Every QA report for a sprint MUST end with a Smoke-Test Checklist block. The sprint is NOT complete until the human operator confirms they have walked through the checklist and found no blocking issues. QA may pass individual tickets based on static analysis, but the sprint-level verdict is PENDING until the smoke test is confirmed.'
3. Define the standard 5-minute smoke-test flow that must appear verbatim (or adapted to the specific sprint's changes) in every report:
   a. Sign up as a new user (or log in as an existing test user).
   b. Feed tab: scroll 3 cards. Confirm vote buttons are visible. Cast a YES vote on any poll card. Pull to refresh. Confirm the vote indicator persists (not wiped).
   c. Markets tab: open any OPEN market. Confirm the sticky bet panel is visible. Place a 1-point bet. Confirm the position summary updates in the sticky bar.
   d. Profile tab: confirm wallet balance updated after the bet. Confirm Bets section shows the bet just placed (not an empty list).
   e. Create tab: start the Simple wizard. Complete all 4 steps. Submit. Confirm the success screen appears with a 'View Market' button.
4. The checklist block in each QA report must use a markdown checkbox format so the human can literally check boxes as they test.
5. Individual ticket verdicts (pass/fail) remain driven by static analysis. The smoke-test checklist is an additional sprint-level gate — it does not retroactively change individual ticket statuses.

tickets.title: Hotfix: mobile register wallet gap — verify fix, backfill integrity, audit all create-user paths, regression test
tickets.description:
## Background

A production bug was discovered and partially remediated out-of-band. The mobile registration route (`apps/api/app/api/auth/mobile/register/route.ts`) was creating users without a wallet record. The web route (`apps/api/app/api/auth/register/route.ts`) correctly creates wallet + stats + notifications in a single `prisma.user.create` call. The mobile route omitted the wallet relation entirely, causing every downstream read of `user.wallet?.balance` to crash with 'Wallet not found'.

**What was done before this ticket:**
- Mobile register route patched: now includes `wallet: { create: { balance: STARTING_BALANCE, startingBalance: STARTING_BALANCE } }`, `stats: { create: {} }`, and `notifications: { create: { ... } }` inside the `prisma.user.create` call.
- Backfill script created and run: `apps/api/scripts/backfill-wallets.ts` — gave wallets to 7 affected users (kiran, kiran1–4, sar1, sar2).

## Acceptance Criteria

### 1. Verify the mobile route fix is fully symmetrical with the web route

Read both routes side-by-side and confirm the mobile route now creates all three relations: `wallet`, `stats`, and `notifications`. Align the mobile welcome notification title to match the web title: change it from `'Welcome!'` to `'Welcome to the news feed'`.

### 2. Verify the backfill ran cleanly

Run a Prisma query to confirm all 7 affected users now have wallets and that NO users without wallets remain in the database.

### 3. Audit all user-creation paths for missing wallet/stats/categoryStats

Three paths: web register, mobile register, seed.ts. Confirm seed.ts has a comment explaining why it intentionally skips the welcome notification.

### 4. Audit wallet-consumer sites for missing-wallet resilience

Files to review: positions/route.ts, bond.ts, create.ts. Add explicit null guards with clear error messages where missing.

### 5. Add a regression test

Create `apps/api/scripts/test-mobile-register.ts` that signs up a fresh test user and asserts wallet + stats + notification were created.

## Definition of Done

- Mobile register route title aligned. Backfill verified clean. Seed script has comment. Wallet-consumer files have null guards. Regression test script exists and is runnable.

tickets.title: Profile empty-state cleanup: suppress hollow cards, add GetStartedCard, reorder activity above P&L, drop Streak tile
tickets.description:
## Strategic framing

Activity + Accuracy is the hero content of the Profile screen. This sprint is Phase 1 of a two-phase Profile redesign. Phase 2 (sub-tabs, consolidated performance card, sticky identity strip) is Sprint 11 and is OUT OF SCOPE here.

This is a **single-file edit**: `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx`. Do not touch any other tab, any API route, or any shared type.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### 1. Suppress empty cards entirely

Sections that must NOT render at all when their data is empty:

- **P&L summary card**: suppress when `pnl === null || pnl.resolvedMarketCount === 0`.
- **Recent Positions card**: suppress when `positions.length === 0`.
- **Poll Votes card** (PredictionsSection or equivalent votes list): suppress when `votes.length === 0`.
- **Badges shelf**: suppress when `badges.length === 0`.
- **Host Stats card**: already conditional on `user.hostStats == null` — verify this guard is present and stays in place. Do not remove it.
- **My Markets**: already conditional — verify and leave.
- **Watchlist**: already conditional — verify and leave.

### 2. Add a single unified GetStartedCard

Render ONLY when positions.length === 0 AND votes.length === 0 AND badges.length === 0 AND (pnl === null || pnl.resolvedMarketCount === 0). Three tappable rows: Make first prediction (Feed), Explore markets (Markets), Join a group (Groups).

### 3. Move Recent Activity above P&L

New render order: Header card > Leaderboard link > Groups preview > Recent Positions > Poll Votes > P&L card > Host Stats > Badges > Category Breakdown.

### 4. Drop Streak tile from stats row

Stats row becomes 3 tiles: Points | Rep | Accuracy. Streak badge above the row stays.

### 5. Hard constraints

No sub-tabs, no sticky strip, no card consolidation. Single-file edit only: profile.tsx.

tickets.title: Sticky identity strip + Performance Strip line
tickets.description:
## Context

Sprint 11 Phase 2 of the Profile screen redesign. Strategic framing: "Activity + Accuracy is the hero content." This ticket restructures the profile header to be sticky and replaces the 3-stat tile row with a compact Performance Strip line.

This is the FIRST of three sequential tickets. T2 (sub-tabs) and T3 (consolidated Performance card) are blocked on this ticket passing human smoke test. Do NOT touch sub-tabs, card consolidation, or anything below the header.

**Single-file edit: `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx`. No API changes. No new types.**

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### 1. Sticky header

The header card containing avatar + username + level/streak tags must become sticky — it must remain visible at the top of the screen when the user scrolls the body content.

Implementation: extract the header into a fixed/non-scrolling element above the ScrollView. The simplest approach is:

```jsx
<View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  {/* Non-scrolling header — always visible */}
  <HeaderCard ... />
  {/* Scrollable body */}
  <ScrollView>...rest of profile content...</ScrollView>
</View>
```

Alternatively, use `stickyHeaderIndices` on a FlatList if the current layout uses one. Either implementation is acceptable as long as the header stays pinned while body content scrolls underneath it.

### 2. Performance Strip line

Replace the current 3-stat tile row (Points | Rep | Accuracy, introduced in S10) with a single horizontal "Performance Strip" text line positioned just below the username.

Format: `{formattedPoints} pts · {positions.length} predictions · {accuracyScore}% accuracy · {netPnl > 0 ? '+' : ''}{netPnl} net`

Where:
- `formattedPoints`: the user's wallet balance formatted with `formatPoints()` or equivalent
- `positions.length`: count of all positions (use the positions array already fetched in the screen)
- `accuracyScore`: the user's accuracy percentage (already on the user object)
- `netPnl`: `pnl?.netPnl ?? 0` — the net P&L already fetched from the API

For users with zero predictions, degrade gracefully to a single-line CTA instead of the strip: "Make your first prediction" (tappable, routes to `/(tabs)/feed`).

Style: single line, small-to-medium font (12–14sp), muted/secondary text color (e.g. `colors.textSecondary` or equivalent), horizontally centered or left-aligned to match the username text above it. The dots (·) are literal Unicode middle-dot separators.

### 3. Points tile removed

The 3-stat tile row (Points | Rep | Accuracy from S10) is fully removed. Points are now represented inside the Performance Strip. Rep and Accuracy are de-emphasized — they still exist on the user object but are no longer shown as prominent tiles.

### 4. Streak tag preserved

The streak tag (fire emoji + N days) stays exactly where it currently is (in the tag row above/beside the Performance Strip). Do NOT move or remove it.

### 5. Avatar, username, level tag preserved

Avatar circle, username text, and level tag all stay. Their visual treatment (dark background, white text on the header card) stays.

### 6. Reputation bar removed

The progress bar visualizing the reputation score is dropped. It consumed vertical space and is not part of the S11 hero layout.

### 7. Out of scope

Do NOT introduce sub-tabs. Do NOT consolidate P&L/Category/Host cards. Do NOT touch anything below the header card in the scroll body.

---

## Definition of Done

- Header is sticky: scrolling the profile body does not move the header card off screen.
- Performance Strip appears below the username with all 4 elements: pts, predictions count, accuracy %, net P&L.
- Zero-predictions users see a tappable CTA instead of the strip.
- Streak tag is unaffected.
- 3-stat tile row is gone. Reputation bar is gone.
- No TypeScript errors.
- No other file modified.

tickets.title: Sub-tabs inside Profile (Activity | Stats | Markets)
tickets.description:
## Context

Sprint 11 Phase 2 of the Profile screen redesign. This is the SECOND of three sequential tickets. **BLOCKED until S11-T1 passes human smoke test on device.** The CEO must manually authorize this ticket before the CTO begins it.

**Single-file edit: `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx`.**

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### 1. Sub-tab bar

Add a sub-tab bar immediately below the sticky identity strip (built in S11-T1). Three tabs: **Activity** (default), **Stats**, **Markets**.

Style: pill-style segmented control matching the existing Markets-screen mode toggle pattern (same component or same styling approach).

### 2. Activity tab content

Merged chronological list of recent positions + poll votes, sorted by createdAt DESC, capped at 30 items. Each row shows:
- Market title
- The user's call (YES / NO / numeric value)
- Outcome icon: checkmark (won), cross (lost), clock (pending resolution)
- Points staked or vote weight

This replaces the current separate `RecentPositions` section and `PredictionsSection` (votes). Those two components are merged into one unified Activity list on this tab.

### 3. Stats tab content

Route today's existing cards here — P&L card + Category Breakdown bars + Host Stats card (when hostStats != null). No consolidation in this ticket — just route them to this tab.

### 4. Markets tab content

Route today's My Markets list + Watchlist here. Same content, just assigned to this tab.

### 5. GetStartedCard placement

The `GetStartedCard` from S10 stays — it renders on the Activity tab only, when fully empty (positions.length === 0 AND votes.length === 0).

### 6. Navigation items stay below tabs

Leaderboard link + Groups preview + Notifications/Logout footer stay BELOW the sub-tabs and their scrollable content. They are always visible regardless of selected sub-tab. Reason: they are navigational, not activity content.

### 7. Per-tab empty states

If a tab's data is empty, show a small friendly message — NOT the GetStartedCard:
- Activity tab (empty but user has other data elsewhere): "No predictions yet. Head to the Feed to get started."
- Stats tab (no resolved P&L): "Complete your first prediction to unlock stats."
- Markets tab (no created markets or watchlist): "Markets you create or watch will appear here."

The GetStartedCard is only for the truly brand-new user state (all four tracked categories empty simultaneously).

### 8. Out of scope

Do NOT consolidate any cards in this ticket. Just route existing cards to the correct tab. T3 handles consolidation.

---

## Definition of Done

- Sub-tab bar renders below the sticky header strip.
- Activity tab shows unified positions + votes list sorted by recency.
- Stats tab shows P&L + Category + Host Stats (when present).
- Markets tab shows My Markets + Watchlist.
- GetStartedCard renders on Activity tab only when fully empty.
- Leaderboard/Groups/footer remain below all tab content.
- Per-tab empty states render correctly.
- No TypeScript errors. No other file modified.

tickets.title: Consolidated Performance card on Stats sub-tab
tickets.description:
## Context

Sprint 11 Phase 2 of the Profile screen redesign. This is the THIRD and final ticket of Sprint 11. **BLOCKED until S11-T2 passes QA and human smoke test.** The CEO must manually authorize this ticket before the CTO begins it.

**Single-file edit: `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx`.**

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### 1. Replace 3 cards with 1 on Stats sub-tab

On the Stats sub-tab (built in S11-T2), replace the three existing separate cards (P&L Summary + Category Breakdown + Host Stats) with **one** consolidated "Performance" card.

### 2. Card content layout

**Row 1 — Dominant net P&L number:**
- Large font, colored green if positive / red if negative / neutral gray if zero
- Subtext below: "Net P&L across resolved predictions"

**Row 2 — 4 stat pills in a 2x2 or 4-column grid:**
- Accuracy % (from `user.accuracyScore`)
- Predictions count (from `positions.length`)
- Win Rate % (wins / total resolved, computed from pnl data)
- Top Category: the category with highest accuracyScore from `categoryStats` (show just the name, e.g. "Sports")

**Row 3 — Category Breakdown (collapsible):**
- Header row: "Category Breakdown" label + expand/collapse chevron
- When expanded: shows the category accuracy bars from today's CategoryBreakdown component
- Collapsed by default

**Row 4 — Host Stats (only when `hostStats != null`, collapsible):**
- Header row: "Host Stats" label + expand/collapse chevron
- When expanded: shows Trust Score / Markets / Clean Streak from today's Host Stats card
- Collapsed by default

### 3. Empty-state treatment

**When user has no resolved predictions** (`pnl === null || pnl.resolvedMarketCount === 0` but user does have some activity — positions or votes exist):
- Render a structured skeleton card that shows the layout in muted gray
- Single CTA inside: "Make 3 predictions to unlock your stats"
- Do NOT render an empty card with no content

**When user is truly brand-new** (`positions.length === 0 AND votes.length === 0`):
- Suppress the Performance card entirely (GetStartedCard is active on Activity tab; no need for a second empty state on Stats)

### 4. Out of scope

Anything outside the Stats sub-tab. Any API changes. Any file other than profile.tsx.

---

## Definition of Done

- Stats sub-tab shows one consolidated Performance card instead of three separate cards.
- Net P&L is color-coded correctly (green/red/neutral).
- 4 stat pills visible in Row 2.
- Category Breakdown and Host Stats sections are collapsible (collapsed by default).
- Skeleton card renders for users with activity but no resolved predictions.
- Card is suppressed entirely for brand-new users.
- No TypeScript errors. No other file modified.

tickets.title: Leaderboard: dynamic subtitle + sort-order consistency fix
tickets.description:
## Problem

The leaderboard subtitle reads "Top predictors by reputation" on every tab regardless of the active category filter. Category tabs (Sports, Business, Tech, General) sort entries by accuracy in that category, but the subtitle never updates to reflect this. The "All" tab sorts by reputation; category tabs sort by accuracy — but the UI labels both identically. This is a trust-eroding inconsistency: users see different rankings with the same label and cannot tell why.

## Acceptance Criteria

### 1. Dynamic subtitle

In `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/leaderboard.tsx`, make the subtitle text reactive to the active category filter:

- When `activeCategory === 'All'`: subtitle = "Ranked by reputation"
- When `activeCategory` is any specific category (Sports, Business, Tech, General): subtitle = "Ranked by accuracy in [Category]"

The subtitle must update immediately (no delay) when the user taps a different category chip.

### 2. Explicit sort-axis label on each entry row

For category tabs, each leaderboard entry row already shows an accuracy percentage. Add a small label above the list (below the subtitle, above the first row) that reads: "Showing [N] top predictors" — this anchors the user's mental model on what they're looking at. This label should also update when the category changes.

### 3. Sort consistency audit

Read `apps/api/app/api/leaderboard/route.ts`. Confirm:
- For `category=all` (or no category param): entries are sorted by `reputationScore DESC`.
- For any specific category: entries are sorted by that category's accuracy score DESC.

If either sort is incorrect or inconsistent, fix it. The API sort must match the UI label — if the API sorts by reputation on category tabs, either fix the API to sort by accuracy or update the subtitle to say "Ranked by reputation" everywhere. The fix must make the sort and the label consistent. Preference: sort category tabs by accuracy (it is more meaningful for category-specific leaderboards).

### 4. No regressions

- The `userRank` banner at the bottom (showing the current user's rank if they are outside the top 50) must still work after this change.
- Category filter chips must still work and trigger a re-fetch.
- The `useFocusEffect` auto-refresh must still work.

## Files likely touched

- `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/leaderboard.tsx` (subtitle logic, count label)
- `apps/api/app/api/leaderboard/route.ts` (sort consistency fix if needed)

## Definition of Done

- Subtitle reads "Ranked by reputation" on All tab and "Ranked by accuracy in [Category]" on category tabs.
- "Showing N top predictors" count label appears below the subtitle.
- API sort matches the displayed label (verified by reading the route handler).
- No TypeScript errors. No unrelated files modified.

tickets.title: Leaderboard: time-window selector (This Week / This Month / All Time)
tickets.description:
## Problem

The leaderboard is a flat all-time ranking. A user who just joined has no competitive foothold — they are permanently buried behind users who have been playing for months. Weekly leaderboards create a fresh competitive context every 7 days and dramatically improve 7-day retention (Duolingo's weekly league mechanic drove 7-day retention from 12% to 55%). This is the single highest-leverage unlock on the Leaderboard screen.

## Acceptance Criteria

### API changes — `apps/api/app/api/leaderboard/route.ts`

1. Add a `timeWindow` query parameter: `'week' | 'month' | 'all'`. Default to `'all'` for backwards compatibility.
2. When `timeWindow=week`: filter leaderboard entries to only include prediction activity (positions placed, votes cast) within the last 7 calendar days. Compute accuracy and reputation delta within that window only.
3. When `timeWindow=month`: same logic, last 30 days.
4. When `timeWindow=all`: existing behavior (no time filter).
5. The `userRank` field in the response must also be scoped to the same time window — the user's rank among all users active in that window, not their all-time rank.
6. If a user has zero activity in the selected window, they do not appear in the list (do not include zero-score entries).

**Note on implementation:** If computing a true windowed accuracy score from raw positions/votes is too complex for one sprint, an acceptable fallback is to filter entries to users who have `lastPredictionAt` within the window and sort them by their existing all-time score. The key deliverable is that the window selector is functional and the list visibly changes between windows — exact within-window score recomputation can be a follow-up.

### Mobile UI changes — `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/leaderboard.tsx`

7. Add a row of three pill/chip selectors below the screen title and above the category chips: **This Week** | **This Month** | **All Time**. Default to **This Week**.
8. The active pill is highlighted (same style as the active category chip).
9. Tapping a pill updates a `timeWindow` state variable and triggers a re-fetch of the leaderboard with the new `timeWindow` param.
10. The subtitle (from S12-T1) must remain accurate: "Ranked by reputation" or "Ranked by accuracy in [Category]" — the time window does not change the sort axis label.
11. While the re-fetch is in progress, show the existing loading indicator (or a subtle opacity fade on the list).

### Type changes

12. Update the `ApiLeaderboardResponse` type (in `packages/api-client/src/types.ts` or wherever it lives) to include `timeWindow` as an optional request param and ensure `userRank` is typed as `number | null`.

## Files likely touched

- `apps/api/app/api/leaderboard/route.ts`
- `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/leaderboard.tsx`
- `packages/api-client/src/types.ts` (or `index.ts`)
- `packages/api-client/src/index.ts` (add `timeWindow` param to `getLeaderboard` call)

## Definition of Done

- Three time-window pills appear on the leaderboard screen, default to This Week.
- Tapping a pill re-fetches the leaderboard and the list visibly changes.
- `userRank` in the response is scoped to the selected window.
- API accepts `timeWindow` param and filters/sorts accordingly.
- No TypeScript errors. No regressions on category filtering or subtitle behavior from S12-T1.

tickets.title: Leaderboard: sticky 'Your Rank' card pinned below selectors
tickets.description:
## Problem

The user's own rank is currently shown as a small banner buried at the bottom of the scrollable list — only visible after scrolling past every other entry. Users who are not in the top 50 have to scroll to the very bottom to find their own position. This is the opposite of motivating: the product should show users exactly where they stand and who they need to beat, immediately and without scrolling.

## Acceptance Criteria

### 1. Move "Your Rank" card to a sticky position

In `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/leaderboard.tsx`, move the user's rank display from the scrollable list footer to a pinned card positioned immediately below the time-window pills and category chips — above the scrollable list of other users.

The card must remain visible while the user scrolls through the leaderboard entries. It does NOT scroll with the list.

Implementation: place the card in a non-scrolling wrapper above the FlatList/ScrollView that contains the ranked entries.

### 2. Card content

The card must show:
- The user's current rank: "You're #[N]" (large, prominent)
- The user directly above them (the target): "@[username] is #[N-1]"
- The gap to the target: "[X] rep behind" (for All tab) or "[X]% accuracy behind" (for category tabs)

Format example for All tab: "You're #52. @alice is #51 — 120 rep behind her."
Format example for category tab: "You're #14 in Sports. @bob is #13 — 8% accuracy behind him."

For computing the gap: the API already returns the full top-50 entries list plus the `userRank`. To get the target user's score, the CTO should also include a `userContext` object in the API response:
```json
{
  "userContext": {
    "rank": 52,
    "score": 1240,
    "targetUsername": "alice",
    "targetRank": 51,
    "targetScore": 1360,
    "gap": 120,
    "gapUnit": "rep"
  }
}
```
Add this `userContext` field to `GET /api/leaderboard` response. If the user IS in the top 50, the card should instead show: "You're #[N] — keep it up!" with no target comparison.

### 3. CTA for unranked users

If the user has no rank yet (zero activity in the selected time window — `userRank === null`):
- Show the card with text: "You're not ranked yet."
- Below that, a tappable CTA button: "Make a prediction" that navigates to `/(tabs)/feed`.
- Do NOT show a gap or target for unranked users.

### 4. Card styling

- The card should be visually distinct from the ranked entries list — use a slightly different background color (e.g. a dark tinted card matching the app's brand color, or a subtle border).
- The user's own entry in the scrollable list below should still be highlighted with the `isCurrentUser` row treatment (already implemented) — this is not removed.
- The sticky card and the highlighted row are both present simultaneously if the user is in the top 50. This is intentional — the sticky card gives at-a-glance rank info; the highlighted row gives rank-in-context.

### 5. API changes — `apps/api/app/api/leaderboard/route.ts`

Add the `userContext` object described above to the leaderboard response. This requires:
1. Fetching the current user's rank (already done for the existing `userRank` field).
2. Fetching the entry ranked one position above the user.
3. Computing the gap between the user's score and the target's score.
4. Returning `userContext: { rank, score, targetUsername, targetRank, targetScore, gap, gapUnit }` or `userContext: null` if the user is unranked.

This endpoint must be authenticated for `userContext` to be populated. Unauthenticated requests return `userContext: null`.

## Files likely touched

- `apps/api/app/api/leaderboard/route.ts`
- `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/leaderboard.tsx`
- `packages/api-client/src/types.ts`

## Definition of Done

- "Your Rank" card is pinned above the scrollable list and visible without scrolling.
- Card shows rank, target username, and gap for ranked users.
- Card shows "Make a prediction" CTA for unranked users.
- `userContext` is returned by the API.
- Card updates correctly when time window or category changes.
- No TypeScript errors. No regressions.

tickets.title: Leaderboard: row chevron, delta badge, and category-aware empty state
tickets.description:
## Problem

Three small polish gaps that each add friction or miss an engagement opportunity:

1. Leaderboard rows are tappable (navigate to public user profile per S8-T5) but have no visual affordance indicating they are tappable.
2. Users cannot tell if their rank improved or declined since last week — there is no movement indicator.
3. The empty state when a category has no entries reads "No entries yet." — generic, cold, and a dead end.

## Acceptance Criteria

### 1. Chevron icon on leaderboard rows

In `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/leaderboard.tsx`, add a right-facing chevron icon (e.g. `chevron-forward` from Ionicons, small, muted color) to the trailing edge of each leaderboard entry row. This is the standard iOS affordance for "tap to go deeper."

The chevron should be consistent across all rows (both the scrollable entries and the sticky "Your Rank" card's target user, if applicable).

### 2. Rank delta badge on the user's own row

If rank history data is available:
- On the user's own highlighted row in the scrollable list, add a small badge showing rank movement: "↑3" (green, moved up 3 spots) or "↓2" (red, moved down 2 spots) or "—" (no change).
- The delta is computed relative to the previous time period of the same window (e.g. last week vs this week if time window is "This Week").

**If rank history does not exist in the current data model:** ship only the chevron. Do NOT fabricate delta data or add placeholder zeros. Add a code comment `// TODO: rank delta badge — requires rank_history table` and skip the badge entirely. The chevron alone is the deliverable if history is absent.

To check: look at the `UserStat` model in `apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma`. If there is no `rankHistory` or `previousRank` field, rank history does not exist — skip the delta badge.

### 3. Category-aware empty state

In `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/leaderboard.tsx`, when the fetched entries list is empty for a given category + time window combination, replace the generic "No entries yet." text with a category-aware message:

- For category tabs: "No predictions in [Category] yet — be the first!" with a tappable "Make a prediction" CTA button that navigates to `/(tabs)/feed`.
- For the All tab with an empty result (edge case — should not normally happen but handle it): "No predictions yet — be the first!"

The CTA button should use the same style as the "Make a prediction" button in the sticky "Your Rank" card (S12-T3) for visual consistency.

### 4. No API changes required

This is a purely mobile-side ticket. No new API endpoints, no schema changes (unless rank history already exists — but based on the scout note above, it likely does not).

## Files likely touched

- `apps/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/leaderboard.tsx`
- `apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma` (read-only — to verify rank history presence)

## Definition of Done

- Chevron icon appears on all leaderboard entry rows.
- Delta badge appears on the user's own row IF rank history exists in the schema; if not, a TODO comment is present and no badge renders.
- Empty state for category tabs shows category-aware CTA instead of "No entries yet."
- No TypeScript errors. No regressions on S12-T1, S12-T2, S12-T3 behavior.
